description: After finding an old letter hidden among her grandmother's belongings, Clara decides to travel to a small mountain town where her family lived decades ago. What begins as a simple attempt to learn more about the past turns into a journey of unexpected friendships, family secrets, and choices that could change her future.

chapters.title: The Forgotten Letter
chapters.content:
Clara had always believed that some stories were meant to remain in the past. Her grandmother used to say that certain memories were like old photographs: beautiful when seen from a distance, but difficult to understand when examined closely. For many years, Clara had paid little attention to those words.

That Sunday afternoon, however, while organizing some old boxes in the room that had belonged to her grandmother, she found something that changed the way she thought. It was a small wooden box covered with a thin layer of dust. Clara did not remember ever seeing it before.

She carefully opened the lid. Inside were old photographs, some coins, a watch that no longer worked, and several folded pieces of paper. At the bottom of the box was a yellowed envelope. Her name was written on the front.

Clara stared at those words for a few seconds.

— For Clara.

The handwriting was her grandmother's.

With slightly trembling hands, she opened the envelope. Inside was a single sheet of paper.

“If you found this letter, the time has probably come for you to learn the story I could never tell. Travel to Vale do Cedro. Look for the old train station. There you will find someone who can explain what happened that night.”

Clara read the message twice.

Vale do Cedro.

She knew the name. It was a small town located in a mountainous region, several hours away. Her grandmother had been born there, but she had always avoided talking about her childhood. Clara had never understood why.

At the end of the letter was a second sentence.

“Do not trust only what people tell you. Some truths have been hidden for a very long time.”

Clara felt a chill.

For a few minutes, she considered putting the letter away again and forgetting about it. After all, her life was in another city, her job occupied most of her time, and she had plans for the coming months. An unexpected trip seemed inconvenient.

But there was one question she could not get out of her mind.

What had happened that night?

That same evening, Clara searched for Vale do Cedro. She found photographs of tree-covered mountains, a small square, an old church, and a railway station that seemed to have been abandoned for decades.

She stared at the photograph of the station for a long time.

The next morning, she bought a bus ticket.

She did not know what she would find in that town. She did not know whom she was supposed to look for. And, most importantly, she did not know why her grandmother had waited so many years to leave that message.

But for the first time in a long time, Clara felt that she was about to discover something truly important.

chapters.title: Vale do Cedro
chapters.content:
The bus arrived in Vale do Cedro shortly after four in the afternoon. Clara got off carrying a small backpack and a suitcase that seemed heavier than it should have been. The air in the town felt different. There was a gentle chill, accompanied by the smell of trees and damp earth.

She looked around the small bus station. There were only a few people waiting for buses, a closed newspaper stand, and a café across the street.

Clara took out her phone and opened the photograph of the old station again.

— The station first — she murmured.

The town seemed much smaller than she had imagined. Some streets were narrow and lined with old houses. Many had small gardens in front, with colorful flowers and trees beginning to lose their leaves.

After walking for almost twenty minutes, Clara reached the central square. In the middle was a stone fountain and, beside it, a large clock showing four forty-five.

That was when she realized she did not know where the station was.

Clara entered a small bakery and decided to ask.

Behind the counter was a gray-haired woman arranging some bread in a basket.

— Excuse me — Clara said. — Do you know where the old train station is?

The woman stopped what she was doing.

For a moment, she seemed surprised.

— The old station?

— Yes.

— Are you from out of town?

Clara hesitated.

— I am. My grandmother was born here.

The woman's expression changed immediately.

— What was her name?

Clara answered.

The woman remained silent.

— Helena.

The name seemed to trigger a memory.

— Helena Duarte?

Clara nodded.

The woman placed both hands on the counter.

— Then you're her granddaughter.

— Did you know my grandmother?

— I knew many people back then. But Helena was different.

Clara's curiosity grew.

— What happened to her?

The woman looked away.

— Some things are better left in the past.

Clara immediately remembered the letter.

Do not trust only what people tell you.

— I found a letter she wrote to me — Clara explained. — She asked me to come to the station.

The woman took a deep breath.

— The station is at the end of Acacias Street. You'll find a small bridge. After the bridge, follow the dirt road. It's not very far.

— Thank you.

When Clara turned to leave, the woman called out:

— Wait.

Clara turned back.

The woman took a piece of paper and wrote down an address.

— If you really want to find out what happened, look for this man. His name is Augusto. He lives near the old church.

Clara put the paper away.

— Does he know about my grandmother?

The woman looked directly at her.

— Augusto knows more than anyone else in this town.

Clara left the bakery even more confused than when she had entered.

The sky was beginning to darken. The mountains surrounding the town were almost black against the horizon.

She decided to find somewhere to spend the night before going to the station.

However, as she walked back toward the square, she had the strange feeling that someone was watching her.

When she looked back, she saw only an empty street.

But at the end of the street, there was a man standing near a tree.

He was holding a closed umbrella and watching Clara.

As soon as he realized that she had seen him, he turned and disappeared around a corner.

chapters.title: The Old Station
chapters.content:
The next morning, Clara woke up before her alarm. She had barely slept during the night. The image of the man standing in the street kept returning to her mind.

She tried to convince herself that he was probably just curious. Small towns were like that. People quickly noticed when someone new arrived.

After breakfast, Clara headed to the old station.

The dirt road began after a small stone bridge. As she continued, the houses disappeared behind her and vegetation took over the path. After a few minutes, she saw the first signs of the station.

The building was larger than it had looked in the photograph. The walls were covered with vines, and several windows were broken. An old sign still hung above the entrance.

VALE DO CEDRO.

Clara went inside.

The interior was dark and smelled of old wood. There were benches covered in dust, an abandoned counter, and a clock stopped exactly at eleven seventeen.

She slowly walked through the hall.

— Is anyone here?

Her voice echoed through the building.

There was no answer.

Clara took the letter from her backpack and read the message again.

“Look for the old station. There you will find someone who can explain what happened that night.”

She looked around.

Maybe she had misunderstood the message.

Then she heard a sound.

Footsteps.

They were coming from a room at the back of the building.

Clara froze.

— Is someone there?

The footsteps stopped.

She thought about leaving, but curiosity overcame fear. She walked to the door and slowly opened it.

The room was empty.

There was only a table, a few boxes, and an open window.

Clara approached the table.

There was an object on it that had clearly not been left there by accident.

A photograph.

She picked it up.

Five people appeared in the photograph in front of the station. Clara immediately recognized her grandmother. She looked very young.

Beside her was a man Clara had never seen before.

Behind them was a small sign with a date.

October 17, 1987.

Clara turned the photograph over.

On the back was a handwritten sentence.

“Some goodbyes are not endings.”

She felt her heart race.

Suddenly, she heard the main door slam.

Clara ran back to the hall.

There was no one there.

But the door was open.

On the floor near the entrance was an envelope.

She walked over and picked it up.

Her name was written on it again.

This time, however, the handwriting was not her grandmother's.

Clara opened the envelope.

Inside was only one sentence.

“You should not have come alone.”

She looked toward the door.

For a few seconds, she considered going back to town.

Then she heard a voice behind her.

— I was waiting for you.

Clara turned quickly.

A man was standing in the hallway.

He had completely white hair and was holding a cane. He looked more than seventy years old.

— Are you Augusto? — Clara asked.

The man nodded.

— I am.

— You knew my grandmother?

Augusto looked at the photograph in her hands.

— I knew Helena better than you can imagine.

Clara took a step forward.

— Then tell me what happened that night.

Augusto closed his eyes for a moment.

— Before that, we need to talk about the man in that photograph.

Clara looked at the image again.

— Who is he?

Augusto answered quietly:

— The man your grandmother loved.

Clara was speechless.

chapters.title: The Man in the Photograph
chapters.content:
Augusto took Clara to a small room at the back of the station. There was a table covered with old maps, yellowed newspapers, and photographs arranged in piles.

He pointed to a chair.

— Sit down. What I'm about to tell you may be difficult to understand.

Clara sat down.

Augusto placed the photograph on the table.

— His name was Daniel.

— Daniel was my grandmother's boyfriend?

— More than that. They planned to leave Vale do Cedro together.

Clara frowned.

— Why?

Augusto remained silent for a few seconds.

— Because Helena was tired of living under her family's rules. Your great-grandfather wanted her to marry another man, someone from an important family in the region. Daniel had no money, no land, and no influence. To them, that was enough to prevent the relationship.

Clara looked at the photograph again.

— And they ran away?

— They tried.

Augusto opened a drawer and took out an old newspaper.

The front page was dated October 1987.

There was a small article in the lower corner.

“Young Man Disappears During Night Journey.”

Clara felt a weight in her chest.

— Daniel disappeared?

— That night, he was waiting for Helena at the station. The train would pass shortly after midnight. Helena was supposed to meet him here.

— But she never came.

— No.

— Why?

Augusto looked at her.

— That was what Helena spent the rest of her life trying to understand.

Clara was confused.

— What do you mean? She didn't know why she couldn't go?

— She received a message saying that Daniel had given up and left on his own.

— Who sent the message?

Augusto did not answer immediately.

He placed another piece of paper on the table.

It was a letter.

Clara recognized her grandmother's handwriting.

“Daniel, if you are reading this, know that I never chose to stay. Someone stopped me from reaching the station. They told me you had left. I only discovered years later that it was a lie.”

Clara looked up.

— Did she discover who did it?

— She believed she had.

— Who?

Augusto walked to the window.

— Your great-grandfather.

Clara remained silent.

— But why didn't my grandmother ever tell anyone?

— Because your great-grandfather threatened Daniel.

— Was he alive?

Augusto nodded.

— At least back then, yes.

Clara felt a chill.

— So what happened to Daniel?

Augusto did not answer.

Instead, he opened a box and took out a second photograph.

It was a picture of an older man standing in front of a small house in another town.

On the back was written:

“Daniel, 1998.”

Clara stared at the photograph.

— He survived.

Augusto nodded slowly.

— Yes.

— So my grandmother knew?

— She found out shortly before she died.

Clara stood up.

— Where is he?

Augusto pointed to an address written on a piece of paper.

— Unless he moved, he still lives there.

Clara took the paper.

— Why didn't my grandmother go find him?

Augusto took a deep breath.

— Because Daniel did not want to see her.

The answer hurt more than Clara expected.

— Why?

— Because for decades he believed Helena had chosen to abandon him.

Clara looked at the photograph once more.

Suddenly, she realized that this story was not only about discovering the past.

It was about two people who had spent their entire lives believing different versions of the same night.

And now she had the chance to discover which one was true.

chapters.title: The Journey North
chapters.content:
Clara left Vale do Cedro that same afternoon. Augusto had explained that the trip to the town where Daniel lived would take almost five hours by bus. She could have waited until the next day, but she felt that every minute mattered.

As the bus traveled along the road, Clara watched the mountains through the window. The sky was covered with heavy clouds, and a light rain began to fall.

She opened her backpack and took out the photograph.

Daniel in 1998.

She tried to imagine what he would be like now. Perhaps he had white hair. Perhaps he was married. Perhaps he had children and grandchildren. Perhaps he no longer remembered Helena.

But there was an even bigger question.

Why had he remained in that region for so many years?

When the bus finally arrived in the small northern town, it was already dark.

Clara got off at the bus station and looked for the address Augusto had given her. After asking a few people, she discovered that the house was almost thirty minutes away on foot.

The rain had become heavier.

She pulled up her hood and started walking.

The streets were almost empty. Some houses had their lights on, but most of the stores were already closed.

When she reached the address, she found a simple house with light-colored walls and a small garden.

There was a light on the porch.

Clara stood by the gate for a few seconds.

Then she knocked.

There was no answer.

She knocked again.

This time, she heard footsteps.

The door slowly opened.

An elderly man appeared.

He was holding a small flashlight.

— Can I help you?

Clara felt her throat go dry.

— Are you Daniel?

The man froze.

His expression immediately changed.

— Who wants to know?

Clara took the photograph from her backpack.

— My name is Clara. I'm Helena's granddaughter.

Daniel said nothing.

For a moment, Clara was certain he would close the door.

But he only looked at the photograph.

— Come in.

The house was simple and tidy. There were books covering the walls and several old photographs on the furniture.

Daniel pointed to a chair.

— Sit down.

Clara obeyed.

He remained standing.

— Is Helena alive?

Clara lowered her eyes.

— No. She died a few months ago.

Daniel closed his eyes.

The expression on his face was impossible to interpret.

— I'm sorry.

Clara took a deep breath.

— She left me a letter.

Daniel looked at her.

— What did it say?

Clara told him everything.

She spoke about the box, the station, Augusto, and the photographs.

Daniel listened without interrupting.

When she finished, he walked to a bookshelf and took out a small metal box.

— Helena believed I never knew the truth.

He opened the box.

Inside were old letters.

— But I found out.

Clara was surprised.

— What did you find out?

Daniel held one of the letters.

— That your great-grandfather was not responsible.

Clara frowned.

— Then who was?

Daniel looked at her for several seconds.

— Your grandmother.

Clara felt as if she had been struck.

— That can't be true.

— I didn't want to believe it either.

He placed the letter on the table.

— But she was the one who wrote the message telling me to leave.

Clara looked at the paper.

— Why?

Daniel took a deep breath.

— Because she believed she was protecting me.

— Protecting you from what?

Daniel answered:

— From something that happened that night and that no one in Vale do Cedro had the courage to tell you about.

chapters.title: The Missing Truth
chapters.content:
Clara spent several seconds unable to speak. The rain hit the windows of Daniel's house, creating a constant and almost hypnotic sound.

— I need to understand — she finally said. — My grandmother wrote a letter saying that someone stopped her from going to the station. Now you're telling me that she herself sent you away.

Daniel nodded.

— Both things are true.

Clara became even more confused.

Daniel picked up one of the letters from the box.

— That night, Helena discovered something that could destroy her family. She discovered that her father was involved in a scheme to drive several families from the land near the town.

— My great-grandfather?

— Yes. But he was not working alone.

Daniel placed another photograph on the table.

It showed several people gathered in front of the Vale do Cedro town hall.

— Helena discovered documents that proved everything. She wanted to take the evidence to the police.

— And what does that have to do with you?

— I knew where she had hidden the documents.

Clara looked at him.

— So you were planning to run away together?

— Yes. But not just to start a new life. We wanted to take the evidence to a larger city, where no one could stop the investigation.

Daniel opened another letter.

— That night, Helena told me to wait at the station. Then she disappeared.

— Because someone stopped her?

— Because she changed her mind.

Clara froze.

— She changed her mind?

— Not exactly. She realized that someone was following you.

Clara felt a chill.

— Me?

— You had not even been born yet. I'm talking about your mother.

Daniel continued:

— Helena discovered that your family was being watched. If she handed over the documents, innocent people could be harmed. So she decided to hide everything.

— And you?

— I thought she had abandoned me.

— For how long?

Daniel smiled sadly.

— For many years.

He explained that he had left Vale do Cedro that night and traveled to another city. For decades, he never looked for Helena again.

— Until you heard that she was sick — Clara said.

Daniel nodded.

— I wanted to go see her. But I didn't have the courage.

Clara looked at the letters scattered across the table.

— And the documents?

Daniel remained silent.

— Where are they?

He pointed to the box.

— I don't know.

— What do you mean?

— Helena never told me where she hid them. But she left a clue.

Daniel took out a folded sheet of paper.

It was an old map of Vale do Cedro.

Clara moved closer.

There was a red mark on the map near the mountains.

— What's here?

— An old wooden house.

— Who lives there?

— No one.

Daniel pointed to a small note in the corner of the map.

“When spring comes, look for where the water disappears.”

Clara immediately recognized the phrase.

It was something her grandmother used to say when she was a child.

At the time, Clara had thought it was just a superstition.

Now she realized that it might have been a clue.

She looked at Daniel.

— I'm going back to Vale do Cedro.

Daniel raised his eyebrows.

— Why?

— To find what my grandmother hid.

He remained silent for a few seconds.

Then he closed the metal box.

— Then I'm going with you.

Clara smiled for the first time since arriving at that house.

The next morning, the two of them would return to the mountains.

But neither of them knew that someone had discovered that Clara had been searching for those answers.

And that person was waiting for them in Vale do Cedro.

chapters.title: Back to the Mountains
chapters.content:
Clara and Daniel arrived in Vale do Cedro late in the afternoon. The journey had been quiet for most of the way. Each seemed lost in their own thoughts, trying to imagine what they would find when they reached the old house mentioned on the map.

When the bus stopped at the small bus station, Clara noticed that the town seemed different. Perhaps it was simply because she now knew part of its history, but the streets seemed to hold secrets around every corner.

Daniel got off first and looked at the mountains.

— It's been many years since I've been back here — he said.

Clara put her backpack on.

— Do you regret it?

He took several seconds to answer.

— I still don't know.

They walked toward the central square. There was more activity than the first time Clara had been there. Some people were talking outside the bakery, children were playing near the fountain, and a group of elderly people occupied the benches beneath the trees.

As soon as they entered the square, Clara noticed something strange.

The woman from the bakery was looking at them.

When she recognized Daniel, she froze.

— You're back — she said.

Daniel simply nodded.

— After all these years.

— Some things need to be resolved — he replied.

The woman looked at Clara.

— And you must be Helena's granddaughter.

Clara confirmed it.

The woman took a deep breath.

— Then perhaps it's finally time to tell you some things.

Before she could continue, a man appeared in the doorway of the bakery.

It was the same man Clara had seen on her first day.

The man with the umbrella.

He watched the three of them for a few seconds and then entered a side street.

Clara pointed discreetly.

— That's him.

Daniel looked in the direction she indicated.

His expression changed.

— You know that man?

— No. But he was watching me when I arrived.

Daniel became serious.

— We need to leave.

The two of them quickly crossed the square.

The woman from the bakery called after them, but Daniel did not stop.

After a few minutes, they reached a small inn where Clara had stayed the first night.

In the room, Daniel opened the map again.

— The house is on the other side of the mountain. If we leave early, we'll arrive before dark.

Clara looked at the red mark.

— And what does “where the water disappears” mean?

Daniel pointed to a small drawing on the map.

— There is an old waterfall. During the dry season, part of the water disappears between the rocks.

— Then that's where it is.

— Probably.

Clara sat on the bed.

— Do you think my grandmother left the evidence there?

Daniel answered:

— I think she wanted someone to find it.

That night, Clara barely slept.

Shortly before midnight, she heard footsteps in the hallway.

She opened her eyes.

The footsteps stopped in front of the door.

For several seconds, no one moved.

Then a piece of paper slid underneath the door.

Clara slowly got up and picked it up.

There was only one sentence written on it:

“Stop looking.”

Clara looked at Daniel.

He was awake.

— I think we know now that we're on the right track — he said.

chapters.title: The Abandoned House
chapters.content:
The next morning, Clara and Daniel left before sunrise. The road to the mountains was narrow and surrounded by tall trees. The sky was still dark when they left the last houses behind.

Daniel carried a backpack with water, food, and a few tools. Clara carried the map carefully protected inside a plastic folder.

After almost two hours of walking, they reached a trail covered with leaves.

— From here on, we have to continue on foot — Daniel said.

The climb was difficult. In some places, the path completely disappeared among the trees. Clara slipped several times, but she continued.

After another hour, they heard the sound of running water.

The waterfall was nearby.

When they arrived, they found a small waterfall flowing between enormous moss-covered rocks. During the rainy season, it was probably much larger.

Daniel opened the map.

— Where the water disappears.

They walked around the waterfall until they found a small passage between the rocks. Behind it was an almost invisible trail.

The trail led to a wooden house.

Clara stopped.

— This is it.

The house was abandoned. Part of the roof had collapsed and the windows were broken. A tree had grown so close to one of the walls that its roots were beginning to lift the floor.

Daniel opened the door.

A strong smell of damp wood filled the room.

There were only a few old pieces of furniture, a fireplace, and an empty bookshelf.

Clara slowly walked through the rooms.

In the main bedroom, she found a small box hidden inside a cabinet.

She opened it.

Inside were photographs, letters, and an old key ring.

Daniel picked up one of the photographs.

It was Helena.

She was standing in front of the same house many years earlier.

On the back was written:

“If I ever need to hide everything, it will be here.”

Clara felt her heart race.

— We found it.

Daniel continued examining the box.

— Not yet.

— What?

He held up one of the letters.

— The evidence isn't here. Only the instructions.

The letter pointed to another location.

“When you find the house, look for the tree that grew on top of the stone.”

Clara immediately went outside.

There were dozens of trees around the house.

Daniel began searching.

After a few minutes, Clara found a huge tree growing over a rocky formation.

— Daniel!

He approached.

There was a small opening between the roots.

Daniel used a tool to move some stones aside.

Behind them was a metal box.

Clara stopped breathing.

The box was locked.

The key ring found in the house had a small key.

Daniel tried it.

The lock opened.

Inside were several old documents.

But there was also something neither of them expected.

A cassette tape.

The label read:

“For whoever finds the truth.”

Clara looked at Daniel.

— How are we going to listen to this?

He answered:

— I know someone in town who might still have a player.

At that moment, they heard a branch break behind them.

They both turned around.

There was no one there.

But someone had left footprints in the wet ground.

And they led directly to the house.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.content:
Clara and Daniel went down the mountain as quickly as they could. Daniel kept the metal box inside his backpack and was careful not to damage any of the documents.

They did not talk about the footprints along the way.

They both knew that someone had followed their trail.

When they reached the town, they went directly to Augusto's house.

The old man was sitting on the porch reading a newspaper.

When he saw the box, he immediately stood up.

— You found it.

Clara placed the box on the table.

— How did you know?

Augusto looked at Daniel.

— Because Helena told me everything.

Daniel was surprised.

— You knew where it was?

— I knew it existed. I never knew exactly where.

Augusto went inside the house and returned a few minutes later carrying an old device.

— It still works.

He put the tape in.

The machine made a low noise before beginning to play.

Then a voice filled the room.

Helena's voice.

Clara felt her eyes fill with tears.

“If you are listening to this recording, it means you finally found the box.”

There was a few seconds of silence.

“I spent many years trying to decide whether I should tell the truth. Perhaps I waited too long.”

Daniel closed his eyes.

“That night, I discovered that the documents my father kept were not only about the land. There were names of people, payments, and secret agreements. Many families were harmed.”

The recording continued.

“I wanted to run away with Daniel. But before reaching the station, I discovered that they were looking for us. I knew that if Daniel was found with the documents, he could be arrested or something worse could happen.”

Clara looked at Daniel.

“So I did the only thing I could think of. I sent him a message saying that I would not go. I knew he would be angry with me. I preferred that he hate me rather than put him in danger.”

Daniel covered his face with one hand.

The voice continued.

“Daniel, if you ever hear this, I need you to know that I never stopped loving you.”

The recording ended for a few seconds.

Then Helena spoke again.

“But there is something you need to know. The documents in the box are not the whole truth. There is a second file. And it contains the name of the person who continued protecting this secret all these years.”

The tape ended.

Nobody spoke.

Finally, Augusto asked:

— Do you understand what this means?

Clara answered:

— There is someone who is still hiding something.

Daniel nodded.

— And that person knows we are looking.

Augusto walked toward the window.

— Then we need to find out who it is before they find out where you are.

Clara opened the metal box.

Among the documents was a sheet of paper with several names.

One of them was circled.

Clara immediately recognized the surname.

It was the surname of one of the most important men in Vale do Cedro.

chapters.title: The Name on the List
chapters.content:
The name circled on the list belonged to Henrique Vasconcelos, one of the wealthiest and most influential men in Vale do Cedro.

Clara knew the surname. In the central square there was a plaque bearing the family's name on an old building. The Vasconcelos family had been involved in the construction of several houses and businesses in the town.

— Who is Henrique Vasconcelos? — Clara asked.

Augusto answered:

— Nowadays? A businessman. He owns several properties in the region.

Daniel examined the document.

— And back then?

— The son of one of the men who worked with your great-grandfather.

Clara felt a chill.

— So he knew everything?

— Perhaps more than that.

Augusto placed another document on the table.

It was a land transfer record.

— After your grandmother disappeared from the town, many properties changed hands. Some families were forced to sell their homes for very low prices.

Clara began to understand.

— And Henrique got some of those properties.

— His family did.

Daniel pointed to a signature.

— I know this signature.

Clara looked at it.

— Whose is it?

— My father's.

Silence returned to the room.

— Was your father involved too? — Clara asked.

Daniel shook his head.

— I don't know. Maybe he signed without knowing everything.

Augusto picked up an envelope.

— There is one more thing.

Inside was a letter sent many years after the events.

The sender was Henrique Vasconcelos.

The letter was short.

“Some stories should remain buried. If the documents are found, we will all have problems.”

Clara felt her heart race.

— Is this letter recent?

— Only eight years old — Augusto replied.

Daniel became serious.

— Then he knew the documents existed.

— Yes.

Clara stood up.

— We need to find him.

Augusto grabbed her arm.

— Not so fast.

— Why?

— Because if Henrique knows you found the documents, he may try to take them back.

Clara looked at the box.

— Then what do we do?

Augusto answered:

— First, we make copies of everything.

Daniel agreed.

— Then we take the documents to someone who can protect them.

Clara thought for a few seconds.

— And the second recording?

Augusto looked at her.

— What?

Clara explained what Helena had said about the second file.

Augusto became concerned.

— If there is a second recording, it is probably somewhere only Helena knew about.

Clara took the map from her backpack.

There was a small mark in the corner that they had not noticed before.

A star drawn near the old church.

Daniel moved closer.

— The church.

Clara nodded.

— We'll go tomorrow morning.

That night, however, before they could rest, someone knocked on Augusto's door.

Three slow knocks.

Nobody moved.

Then came three more.

Daniel signaled for Clara to stay behind him.

Augusto turned off the lights.

A voice came from outside.

— I know you found the box.

Clara recognized the voice.

It was the man who had been watching her since she arrived.

Henrique Vasconcelos.

chapters.title: The Visit
chapters.content:
No one answered the door.

Outside, Henrique remained silent for a few seconds.

— I'm not here to cause trouble — he said. — I just want to talk.

Daniel approached the window and looked discreetly outside.

Henrique was alone.

— How do you know we're here? — Daniel asked.

— Vale do Cedro is a small town. News travels quickly.

Clara felt a mixture of fear and anger.

— You have been following me since I arrived.

Henrique looked toward the window.

— I needed to know what Helena had left for you.

— Why?

— Because some things can destroy entire families.

Daniel opened the door just enough to talk.

— You knew that Helena and I planned to run away together?

Henrique became serious.

— I knew.

— You knew about the documents?

— Yes.

Clara took a step forward.

— Then why did you never tell the truth?

Henrique looked at her.

— Because I was young and afraid.

— And afterward?

— Afterward it became more difficult. Every year that passed made it harder to go back.

Daniel opened the door completely.

— Do you know where the second file is?

Henrique took a deep breath.

— I do.

Clara felt her heart beat faster.

— Where?

— In the church.

Daniel looked at the map.

— The mark.

Henrique nodded.

— Helena left the second file inside the bell tower.

— Then why didn't you ever get it? — Clara asked.

Henrique took a moment to answer.

— Because I couldn't get inside.

Clara frowned.

— Why?

— Because Helena didn't just hide the documents. She hid a key. Without it, the compartment won't open.

Daniel asked:

— Where is the key?

Henrique looked directly at Clara.

— With you.

Clara felt a chill.

She thought about the small box found in the abandoned house.

At the bottom of it was an object she had not recognized.

A small silver pendant.

Clara took the pendant from her backpack.

Henrique went pale.

— That's it.

Daniel took the object.

On the back was a small star-shaped mark.

The same star drawn on the map.

— Then tomorrow we'll go to the church — Clara said.

Henrique shook his head.

— No.

— Why?

— Because someone got there before us.

At that moment, a bell rang in the distance.

Once.

Twice.

Three times.

Henrique looked toward the church.

— That shouldn't be happening.

Daniel became serious.

— What does it mean?

Henrique answered:

— Someone is inside.

chapters.title: The Bell Tower
chapters.content:
The church of Vale do Cedro stood on top of a small hill. During the day, it was one of the quietest places in town. That night, however, it seemed completely different.

Clara walked beside Daniel, while Henrique followed a few steps behind.

The main door was open.

No lights were on.

— Maybe we should wait until tomorrow — Henrique said.

Daniel looked at him.

— If someone is inside, waiting may be exactly what that person wants.

They went inside.

The interior of the church was dark. The only light came from the moon shining through the stained-glass windows.

Clara could smell old wood and candle wax.

At the back was a narrow staircase leading to the tower.

They began climbing.

With every step, the sound of their footsteps echoed through the empty space.

On the third floor, they found a locked door.

Clara held the pendant.

There was a small opening in the center of the lock.

She inserted the pendant.

There was a click.

The door opened.

Behind it was a small room.

In the center stood an old wooden cabinet.

Daniel opened the doors.

Inside was a box of documents.

Clara took a deep breath.

— We found it.

But before she could touch the box, a light came on behind them.

A man was standing in the doorway.

It was not Henrique.

Nor Augusto.

It was someone Clara knew.

Her own father.

— Dad?

He looked at her with a sad expression.

— Clara, you shouldn't be here.

She did not understand.

— How did you know?

He did not answer.

Daniel stepped forward.

— You knew everything?

Clara's father closed his eyes.

— I knew your grandmother wanted you to find the truth.

— And you tried to stop me?

— No.

He looked at Henrique.

— But some people tried.

Henrique stood still.

— So you knew — he said.

— I found out a few months ago.

Clara felt a mixture of relief and anger.

— Why didn't you tell me?

— Because your grandmother asked me not to.

— Why?

— Because she wanted you to decide for yourself whether you wanted to know the past.

Clara looked at the box.

— And now?

Her father walked toward the cabinet.

— Now you need to decide what to do with it.

He opened the box.

There were dozens of documents.

But at the bottom was one final letter.

Clara immediately recognized the handwriting.

She opened it.

“Clara, if you have made it this far, it means you decided to learn the truth. I want you to know that I never wanted the past to control your life. I only wanted you to have the opportunity to know it before deciding what to do with it.”

Clara continued reading.

“There are things that need to be revealed. But there are also people who have spent years trying to repair the mistakes of their ancestors. Do not turn the truth into revenge.”

At the end there was only one sentence.

“Now the choice is yours.”

Clara closed her eyes.

She finally understood why her grandmother had waited so long.

The story did not end with the discovery of the documents.

In fact, that was where the hardest part began.

Because now Clara had to decide whether she should reveal everything to the world or protect people who were not responsible for what their ancestors had done.
